title: Why Excessive Slope Ruins Gravity Drainage
description: A common misconception in drainage installation is that a steeper pipe pitch always improves flow. In gravity drainage systems, proper function depends on carrying solid waste suspended within liquid flow. If horizontal drainage piping is installed with excessive slope, liquids rapidly outpace heavy solids, leaving debris stranded along the pipe invert. Over time, these dry deposits accumulate and cause severe blockages. Proper slope achieves a self-scouring velocity where liquids and solids transport together predictably. Always check pitch requirements in your local plumbing code and verify gradient using a reliable torpedo level during installation.

Why Excessive Slope Ruins Gravity Drainage

A common misconception in drainage installation is that a steeper pipe pitch always improves flow. In gravity drainage systems, proper function depends on carrying solid waste suspended within liquid flow. If horizontal drainage piping is installed with excessive slope, liquids rapidly outpace heavy solids, leaving debris stranded along the pipe invert. Over time, these dry deposits accumulate and cause severe blockages. Proper slope achieves a self-scouring velocity where liquids and solids transport together predictably. Always check pitch requirements in your local plumbing code and verify gradient using a reliable torpedo level during installation.
